# Adjudication Task — Chapter 57

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃57화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“빨리, 더 빨리!”
  6|
  7|“헉, 허억!”
  8|
  9|우리는 그야말로 미친 듯이 달렸다. 혁무진은 당장 죽을 것처럼 헐떡거렸지만 죽지는 않았다. 발걸음이 느려질 때마다 등에 창날을 가져다 댔더니 적토마가 따로 없더라.
 10|
 11|그리고 어느 순간, 소리가 들리기 시작했다.
 12|
 13|누군가의 비명 소리, 철과 철이 부딪치는 소리…….
 14|
 15|다행이다. 전투는 아직 끝나지 않았다.
 16|
 17|안도감과 동시에 심장이 쿵쿵 뛰었다. 전투는 계속되고 있지만 진위경의 생사는 아직 확인하지 못했다.
 18|
 19|일 분, 일 초 차이로 그가 죽는다면?
 20|
 21|‘만약 그렇다면.’
 22|
 23|까드득.
 24|
 25|나도 모르게 창을 쥔 손에 힘이 들어갔다. 단전에서 끌어올린 공력을 두 다리로 흘려보냈다.
 26|
 27|“조, 조장!”
 28|
 29|빠르게 멀어져 가는 정찰조원들의 목소리를 뒤로하고 계속해서 달렸다. 앞서 본대가 새겨 놓은 무수한 족적, 점점 가까워지는 전장의 소음이 이정표였다.
 30|
 31|‘살아 있어라. 살아 있어라. 제발 살아…….’
 32|
 33|아! 비로소 보인다.
 34|
 35|야트막한 언덕 아래, 불과 200여 미터도 떨어지지 않은 그곳에서 수많은 무인들이 죽고 죽이는 혈전을 벌이고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“죽엇!”
 38|
 39|“으아악!”
 40|
 41|시체와 피, 그리고 더 많은 시체, 피!
 42|
 43|순간 할 말을 잃을 정도로 눈앞에 펼쳐진 광경은 잔혹했다.
 44|
 45|헌터 생활을 통해 내성을 기르지 않았다면 아마 한참 동안이나 충격에서 헤어 나오지 못했을 것이다.
 46|
 47|‘진위경! 진위경은 어디 있지?’
 48|
 49|하지만 가장 먼저 눈에 들어온 사람은 따로 있었다.
 50|
 51|멀리서도 한눈에 들어오는 백발.
 52|
 53|‘대장로!’
 54|
 55|그는 검을 들고 누군가의 앞에 서 있었다.
 56|
 57|대장로의 등에 가려 잘 보이지는 않았지만 무릎을 꿇은 그는 거구의 소유자였고, 손에는 검을 쥔 채였다.
 58|
 59|‘큰 덩치와 검?’
 60|
 61|한 사람밖에 생각나지 않았다.
 62|
 63|진위경이다. 그를 구하려면 당장 움직여야 한다.
 64|
 65|‘인벤토리 오픈.’
 66|
 67|무림에서 사용하는 인벤토리에는 온갖 물건으로 가득했다.
 68|
 69|창대는 나무로, 창두는 강철로 만들어진 이 창도 그중 하나다.
 70|
 71|‘무기 장착.’
 72|
 73|새로 꺼낸 창을 들고 뒤로 몇 걸음 물러났다.
 74|
 75|200여 미터. 까마득한 거리다. 투창으로 누군가를 맞추기에는 더더욱. 하지만 해내야 한다.
 76|
 77|‘못 할 것도 없지.’
 78|
 79|근력, 체력, 민첩.
 80|
 81|무림과 현실을 오가며 키워 온 능력치를 한껏 끌어 올렸다.
 82|
 83|공력이 깃든 팔은 창을 좀 더 멀리, 강하게 쏘아 보낼 수 있을 것이다.
 84|
 85|“후웁.”
 86|
 87|숨을 멈추고 발을 디뎠다. 첫발은 천천히, 마지막 한 걸음은 무겁게. 채찍처럼 휘두른 손끝에서 창대가 쏘아졌다.
 88|
 89|쐐애애액-!
 90|
 91|투창은 내 예상보다 빠르고 정확했다. 금방이라도 대장로의 등을 꿰뚫을 것 같았다.
 92|
 93|그런데…….
 94|
 95|서걱.
 96|
 97|‘뭐야, 저거.’
 98|
 99|푸른빛이 번쩍하더니 창이 두 쪽으로 갈라졌다. 가장 윗부분인 창두부터 끝까지, 깔끔하게.
100|
101|내가 던진 게 창인지 생일 케이크인지 헷갈릴 정도다.
102|
103|“웬 놈이냐!”
104|
105|노인네가 목청도 좋다.
106|
107|“나다, 이 십새끼야!”
108|
109|아마 대장로 평생 들어 본 적 없는 욕일 것이다.
110|
111|심지어 무림에서 그와 나는 한 집안 사람이고, 족보로 따지자면 시조새와 병아리 정도의 항렬 차이가 있다.
112|
113|이것만 해도 당황할 이유는 충분한데, 내게는 결정적인 한 방이 남아 있었다.
114|
115|“대장로는!”
116|
117|공력이 담긴 목소리가 쩌렁쩌렁 울렸다. 목소리를 낸 나도 놀랄 정도인데 다른 이들이 듣기에는 어떨까.
118|
119|저 멀리, 차가운 표정으로 굳은 그를 응시하며 있는 힘껏 외쳤다.
120|
121|“배신자다!”
122|
123|
124|
125|* * *
126|
127|
128|
129|진위경이 그 목소리를 들은 것은 항산검문의 절정 고수 세 명을 모두 쓰러트린 직후였다.
130|
131|아니, 진위경뿐만 아니라 전장의 모두가 그 외침을 들었다.
132|
133|- 웬 놈이냐!
134|
135|- 나다, 이 십새끼야!
136|
137|욕?
138|
139|전장에서는 흔한 일이다. 그러나 욕설의 대상이 대장로라면, 난데없이 나타나 쌍욕을 퍼부은 청년이 진태경이라면 이야기가 달라진다.
140|
141|“저거, 저거 삼공자 아냐?”
142|
143|“뭣? 저놈이 진태경? 그런데 왜?”
144|
145|“이게 무슨 일이야?”
146|
147|진위경도 같은 생각을 했다.
148|
149|‘무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는 거지?’
150|
151|후방에 있어야 할 막내가 전장에 나타났다. 그것만으로도 당황스러운데, 가문의 웃어른에게 입에 담지도 못할 폭언을 쓰기까지 했다. 옆에 있던 위팽이 중얼거렸다.
152|
153|“단단히 미쳤군.”
154|
155|진위경이 저도 모르게 고개를 끄덕이려던 순간.
156|
157|- 대장로는!
158|
159|더 거대한 폭탄이 떨어졌다.
160|
161|- 배신자다!
162|
163|전장이 싸늘한 침묵에 잠겼다. 간간이 들려오던 병장기 부딪치는 소리도 뚝 끊겼다.
164|
165|모두가 멍한 표정으로 진태경을 바라봤다.
166|
167|‘이게 무슨 개소리야?’
168|
169|‘배신? 대장로님께서?’
170|
171|‘취한 거 아냐? 삼공자 저거 옛날 버릇 또 튀어나오네.’
172|
173|태원진가의 무사는 말할 것도 없었고, 항산검문의 무사들도 비슷한 생각을 품었다.
174|
175|최근 들어 진태경을 좋게 보기 시작한 중진들도 입을 딱 벌렸다.
176|
177|“저런 미친놈.”
178|
179|“노야께서 어떤 분이신 줄 알고!”
180|
181|이 전쟁의 일등 공신을 꼽으라면 단연 대장로다.
182|
183|진위경을 도와 가문의 힘을 결집시켰고 오늘 전투에서는 이천백을 꺾었다.
184|
185|이처럼 이번 전쟁의 단순한 공(公)을 떠나 생각해 봐도 진태경의 말은 헛소리로 들릴 수밖에 없었다.
186|
187|대장로가 누군가?
188|
189|화양검이라 불리며 중원에까지 이름을 떨친 전대의 고수요, 정마대전에서 수많은 마두를 쓰러트린 의기의 표상이다.
190|
191|산서성의 무인이라면 누구나 그에게 크고 작은 존경심을 품고 있었다.
192|
193|“그런 분을, 뭐? 십새끼? 배신자?”
194|
195|“허어, 저놈이 태원진가 삼백 년 역사에 똥칠을 하는구나.”
196|
197|태원진가, 항산검문. 이 자리의 모두가 같은 생각을 품은 듯했다. 그러나 적어도 한 사람은 예외였다.
198|
199|‘대장로, 배신.’
200|
201|막내의 말을 들은 순간, 진위경은 온몸의 피가 싸늘하게 식는 것을 느꼈다. 그건 실체를 드러낸 위화감이었다.
202|
203|‘이소군의 죽음이 시작이었지.’
204|
205|그는 극독에 중독되어 죽었다. 항산검문은 태원진가를 범인으로 지목했고, 그것이 전쟁의 시발점이다.
206|
207|하지만 가장 중요한 의문은 빠져 있었다.
208|
209|‘흉수는 누구인가?’
210|
211|전쟁이 막바지에 이른 지금까지도 배후에 숨겨진 흉수에 대해서는 밝혀지지 않았다. 아니, 막바지에 다다랐기 때문에 아무도 흉수의 정체를 신경 쓰지 않았다.
212|
213|적자생존. 강한 자가 살아남아 모든 것을 독식할 테니까.
214|
215|‘이 전쟁은…… 처음부터 잘못된 거였어.’
216|
217|이소군의 죽음. 비상식적으로 빠른 소문의 확산.
218|
219|항산검문이 전쟁을 선언했고, 태원진가가 대응하면서 본격적인 싸움이 시작되었다.
220|
221|‘그리고 대장로가 있었다.’
222|
223|두문불출하던 대장로가 나타난 것은 이소군의 독살 소식이 전해진 직후다. 가문 내에서 그의 역할은 지대했다.
224|
225|존경받는 무인, 가문의 웃어른.
226|
227|대장로가 적극 협조하지 않았다면 태원진가는 둘로 갈라졌을지도 모른다.
228|
229|‘그의 도움 덕분에 여기까지 올 수 있었다.’
230|
231|진위경은 반대로 생각했다.
232|
233|‘여기까지 올 수 있었던 것은, 대장로가 원했기 때문이다.’
234|
235|촌각(寸刻)이라 부르지도 못할 만큼 짧은 순간. 모든 생각을 끝마친 진위경의 입이 열렸다.
236|
237|“위팽.”
238|
239|“하명하십시오.”
240|
241|“일장로를 베어라.”
242|
243|“뭐라?”
244|
245|허리가 구부정하고 깡마른 노인, 일장로가 눈을 부릅떴다.
246|
247|그뿐만 아니라 주위에 있던 중진들 모두가 깜짝 놀랐다.
248|
249|“소, 소가주!”
250|
251|“이 무슨……!”
252|
253|그러나 위팽은 망설이지 않았다. 부지불식간에 휘두른 검이 일장로의 가슴을 향해 날아갔다.
254|
255|카가가각.
256|
257|그때 갑자기 끼어든 두 개의 검이 위팽의 검을 밀어 냈다.
258|
259|뚱뚱하고 키가 훌쩍 큰 두 명의 노인.
260|
261|일장로와 함께 대장로의 수족을 자처하는 이, 삼장로였다.
262|
263|그들의 검에 맺힌 희미한 검기를 확인한 위팽의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
264|
265|“무공을 숨겼군.”
266|
267|대답 대신 일장로의 일권(一拳)이 날아왔다.
268|
269|쾅!
270|
271|살아온 세월만큼이나 심후한 공력으로 위팽을 날려 보낸 일장로가 허리를 곧게 폈다.
272|
273|평생을 대장로의 그늘에 가려져 있었던 또 다른 절정 고수의 등장에 장내가 얼어붙었다.
274|
275|“일장로님, 이, 이게 도대체.”
276|
277|“그럼 혹시!”
278|
279|배신. 그 두 글자가 모두의 뇌리에 선명하게 박혔다.
280|
281|“말도 안 되는 소리!”
282|
283|빽 소리친 사람은 백호당주였다. 대장로의 수족이 장로들이라면 그는 일장로의 손발 노릇을 톡톡히 해냈다.
284|
285|“어르신, 그리고 소가주. 뭔가 오해가 있으신 모양인데…….”
286|
287|그러나 그의 말은 끝까지 이어지지 못했다. 일장로의 턱짓과 동시에 이장로가 눈부신 속도로 백호당주의 목을 베었기 때문이었다.
288|
289|서걱. 툭.
290|
291|진위경과 일장로의 시선이 허공에서 부딪쳤다.
292|
293|“백호당주도 포섭한 게 아니었나?”
294|
295|“시끄러운 놈이었네. 그뿐이야. 다른 놈들도 마찬가지고.”
296|
297|진위경의 예상은 반은 맞고 반은 틀렸다.
298|
299|장로들이 배신한 것은 맞지만, 장로파에 속한 중진들은 배신하지 않았다.
300|
301|“그럼 왜…… 아!”
302|
303|“영민하군. 칭찬해 줌세.”
304|
305|일장로가 품에서 거무튀튀한 죽통(竹筒)을 꺼내 들었다. 이미 타들어 가고 있는 심지가 얼마 남지 않았다.
306|
307|“저런 놈들에게 중요한 비밀을 말해 줄 수야 있나. 내부만 혼란스럽게 만들어도 쓰임새는 다한 거지. 밖에서 무슨 일이 벌어지는지 몰라야 일이 편했으니까.”
308|
309|진위경이 비명처럼 외쳤다.
310|
311|“막아!”
312|
313|“늦었네.”
314|
315|일장로의 말이 맞았다. 심지가 끝까지 타들어 간 순간, 무언가 터지는 소리와 함께 붉은 불꽃이 하늘 높이 솟구쳤다.
316|
317|쉬이익, 펑!
318|
319|그것이 신호였다.
320|
321|세 개의 문파 연합체인 삼도문, 도를 중심으로 수련하는 벽도문, 절벽에서 쉴 새 없이 화살을 쏘아 대던 궁귀문까지.
322|
323|이른바 산서오문이라 불리는 중소 문파의 무인들이 한순간에 돌변했다.
324|
325|“닥치는 대로 죽여라!”
326|
327|“가릴 것 없다! 모두 쓸어 버려라!”
328|
329|그들은 더 이상 어설픈 삼류 무인들이 아니었다. 눈에서는 살기가 흘렀고 검로는 날카로웠다.
330|
331|‘하루아침에 준비한 일이 아니다.’
332|

If anyone deserved the most credit for this war, it was undoubtedly the Head Elder.

[P90]
He had helped Jin Wikyung unite the family’s forces, and in today’s battle, he had defeated Lee Cheonbaek.

[P91]
Even setting aside his contributions to the war, Jin Taekyung’s claim could only sound absurd.

[P92]
Who was the Head Elder?

[P93]
He was a master of the previous generation whose title, the Blade of Flowers, was renowned even across the Central Plains. He was a symbol of righteousness who had struck down countless fiends during the Great Faction War.

[P94]
Every martial artist in Shanxi held some measure of respect for him.

[P95]
“That man? A son of a bitch? A traitor?”

[P96]
“Good heavens. That boy is smearing shit over the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s three-hundred-year history.”

[P97]
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect—everyone present seemed to share the same thought.

[P98]
With at least one exception.

[P99]
*The Head Elder. Betrayal.*

[P100]
The moment Jin Wikyung heard his youngest brother’s words, he felt all the blood in his body run cold.

[P101]
The vague sense that something was wrong had finally taken shape.

[P102]
*Lee Seogeun’s death was where it began.*

[P103]
He had died after being poisoned with a lethal toxin. The Mount Heng Sword Sect had named the Jin Family of Taiyuan as the culprit, sparking the war.

[P104]
But the most important question had been left unanswered.

[P105]
*Who was the killer?*

[P106]
Even now, with the war nearing its end, the culprit hiding behind it all had never been identified. No—precisely because the war was nearing its end, no one cared about the killer’s identity anymore.

[P107]
Survival of the fittest. The strong would survive and claim everything.

[P108]
*This war… was wrong from the very beginning.*

[P109]
Lee Seogeun’s death.

[P110]
The unnaturally rapid spread of the rumors.

[P111]
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had declared war, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had responded. That was how the fighting had begun in earnest.

[P112]
*And the Head Elder was there.*

[P113]
The Head Elder, who had shut himself away from the world, had emerged immediately after news of Lee Seogeun’s poisoning reached the family. His role within the family had been enormous.

[P114]
A respected martial artist. A revered elder of the family.

[P115]
Without the Head Elder’s active support, the Jin Family of Taiyuan might have split in two.

[P116]
*We made it this far because of his help.*

[P117]
Then Jin Wikyung turned the thought around.

[P118]
*We made it this far because this was exactly what the Head Elder wanted.*

[P119]
In a moment too brief to even call an instant, Jin Wikyung reached his conclusion and spoke.

[P120]
“Wipeng.”

[P121]
“Your orders.”

[P122]
“Cut down the First Elder.”

[P123]
“What?”

[P124]
The stooped, emaciated old man—the First Elder—stared wide-eyed.

[P125]
The senior members nearby were equally shocked.

[P126]
“L-Lesser Family Head!”

[P127]
“What is the meaning of this…?”

[P128]
But Wipeng did not hesitate. Before anyone could react, his sword was already flying toward the First Elder’s chest.

[P129]
Clang-clang-clang!

[P130]
Two swords suddenly cut in and knocked Wipeng’s blade aside.

[P131]
Their wielders were two enormously tall, fat old men.

[P132]
They were the Second and Third Elders, who, together with the First Elder, called themselves the Head Elder’s hands and feet.

[P133]
Wipeng’s brow twitched when he saw the faint Sword Energy clinging to their blades.

[P134]
“You were hiding your martial arts.”

[P135]
The First Elder answered with a punch.

[P136]
Boom!

[P137]
The profound internal energy he had accumulated over his long life sent Wipeng flying. Then the First Elder straightened his stooped back.

[P138]
The entire field froze at the emergence of yet another Peak master, one who had spent his life hidden in the Head Elder’s shadow.

[P139]
“First Elder, what… what is this?”

[P140]
“Then could it be…?”

[P141]
*Betrayal.*

[P142]
The word stamped itself into everyone’s mind.

[P143]
“That’s impossible!”

[P144]
The White Tiger Hall Leader let out a shrill shout. If the Elders were the Head Elder’s hands and feet, then he had served faithfully as the First Elder’s.

[P145]
“Elder, Lesser Family Head. There seems to have been some misunderstanding…”

[P146]
But he never finished.

[P147]
The First Elder jerked his chin, and the Second Elder moved with blinding speed, severing the White Tiger Hall Leader’s neck.

[P148]
Shhk. Thud.

[P149]
Jin Wikyung and the First Elder locked eyes across the space between them.

[P150]
“You didn’t recruit the White Tiger Hall Leader?”

[P151]
“He was loud. That was all. The others were no different.”

[P152]
Jin Wikyung’s guess had been half right and half wrong.

[P153]
The Elders had betrayed them, but the senior members of the Elders’ faction had not.

[P154]
“Then why… Ah!”

[P155]
“Sharp. I’ll give you that.”

[P156]
The First Elder drew a dark, grimy bamboo tube from inside his robes. The fuse was already burning, and almost nothing remained.

[P157]
“How could we share such an important secret with men like them? Their job was done once they’d thrown the family into confusion. It made things easier if they had no idea what was happening outside.”

[P158]
Jin Wikyung screamed, “Stop him!”

[P159]
“You’re too late.”

[P160]
The First Elder was right.

[P161]
The moment the fuse burned to its end, something burst, and a red flame shot high into the sky.

[P162]
Fwish—boom!

[P163]
It was a signal.

[P164]
The martial artists of the small and mid-sized sects collectively known as the Five Gates of Shanxi changed in an instant—the Samdo Sect, an alliance of three sects; the saber-focused Byeokdo Sect; and the Gunggui Sect, which had been raining arrows down from the cliffs without pause.

[P165]
“Kill everyone in your path!”

[P166]
“No exceptions! Wipe them all out!”

[P167]
They were no longer the clumsy Third Rate martial artists they had pretended to be. Killing intent poured from their eyes, and their sword paths were razor-sharp.

[P168]
*This wasn’t something they prepared overnight.*

[P169]
Jin Wikyung’s expression hardened.

[P170]
* * *

[P171]
Boom!

[P172]
The Head Elder looked up at the sky. Before the red flame had even faded, thunderous shouts erupted from every direction.

[P173]
*Too fast. Far too fast.*

[P174]
The signal was supposed to be sent only after the Mount Heng Sword Sect had been annihilated. The Five Gates of Shanxi were a blade honed over decades. It had to be swung once and bring everything to a lightning-fast end.

[P175]
*All things have their proper flow.*

[P176]
The plan that had proceeded without a hitch was beginning to unravel.

[P177]
As the Head Elder smiled bitterly, a voice reached his ears.

[P178]
“So… it was you.”

[P179]
Lee Cheonbaek.

[P180]
His voice was faint, but his eyes burned more fiercely than ever.

[P181]
“You still have the strength to speak?”

[P182]
“I’ll tear you apart while you’re still alive.”

[P183]
No sooner had Lee Cheonbaek finished speaking than blood gushed from his mouth. The Head Elder pressed one of his acupoints and murmured, “That would be inconvenient just yet. You still have something to do.”

[P184]
Lee Cheonbaek despaired.

[P185]
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered heavy losses, but several hundred martial artists still remained. With its entire leadership destroyed, if the Sect Leader were now taken prisoner…

[P186]
*Just kill me!*

[P187]
The anguished cry never left his mouth. The Head Elder pressed his Mute Acupoint, robbing him of speech, then brushed the Paralysis Acupoint and turned his body rigid.

[P188]
Lee Cheonbaek had become a living corpse with his eyes wide open.

[P189]
“You bastard! Get your hands off him!”

[P190]
At the same moment, something shrieked through the air.

[P191]
Fwoooosh!

[P192]
The Head Elder did not panic. He swept his sword upward from below. Beyond the spear splitting in two along the line of his Sword Energy, Jin Taekyung was charging toward him at terrifying speed.

[P193]
“Aaaaaah!”

[P194]
“Captain! Please slow down!”

[P195]
And with him came a dozen or so riffraff who had appeared from who knew where.

[P196]
[^1]: Red Hare is the legendary warhorse of Lü Bu in *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). * wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

My voice, loaded with internal energy, thundered across the battlefield. Even I was startled by how loud it was. I could only imagine what it sounded like to everyone else.

[P60]
I stared at his cold, frozen face in the distance and shouted with all my might.

[P61]
“A traitor!”

[P62]
* * *

[P63]
Jin Wikyung heard the voice immediately after bringing down all three Peak masters of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.

[P64]
No, it wasn’t just him. Everyone on the battlefield heard the shout.

[P65]
“Who the hell are you?”

[P66]
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”

[P67]
Cursing?

[P68]
That was common enough on a battlefield. But it was a different matter when the target was the Head Elder and the young man who had appeared out of nowhere to hurl such abuse at him was Jin Taekyung.

[P69]
“Isn’t that… the Third Young Master?”

[P70]
“What? That’s Jin Taekyung? But why?”

[P71]
“What’s going on?”

[P72]
Jin Wikyung was wondering the same thing.

[P73]
*What in the world is happening?*

[P74]
His youngest brother, who should have been in the rear, had appeared on the battlefield. That alone was bewildering enough, but now he was hurling unspeakable abuse at one of the family’s most senior elders.

[P75]
Wipeng, standing beside him, muttered, “He’s completely lost his mind.”

[P76]
Jin Wikyung was about to nod without thinking when—

[P77]
“The Head Elder is—!”

[P78]
An even bigger bomb dropped.

[P79]
“A traitor!”

[P80]
An icy silence fell over the battlefield. Even the sporadic clash of weapons came to an abrupt stop.

[P81]
Everyone stared blankly at Jin Taekyung.

[P82]
*What kind of bullshit is this?*

[P83]
*Betrayal? The Head Elder?*

[P84]
*Is he drunk? The Third Young Master must be slipping back into his old habits.*

[P85]
The martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan naturally thought so, and those of the Mount Heng Sword Sect were no different.

[P86]
Even the senior members who had recently begun to think better of Jin Taekyung gaped at him.

[P87]
“What a lunatic.”

[P88]
“Does he have any idea who the Old Master is?”

[P89]
If anyone deserved the most credit for this war, it was undoubtedly the Head Elder.

[P90]
He had helped Jin Wikyung unite the family’s forces, and in today’s battle, he had defeated Lee Cheonbaek.

[P91]
Even setting aside his contributions to the war, Jin Taekyung’s claim could only sound absurd.

[P92]
Who was the Head Elder?

[P93]
He was a master of the previous generation whose title, the Blade of Flowers, was renowned even across the Central Plains. He was a symbol of righteousness who had struck down countless fiends during the Great Faction War.

[P94]
Every martial artist in Shanxi held some measure of respect for him.

[P95]
“That man? A son of a bitch? A traitor?”

[P96]
“Good heavens. That boy is smearing shit over the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s three-hundred-year history.”

[P97]
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect—everyone present seemed to share the same thought.

[P98]
With at least one exception.

[P99]
*The Head Elder. Betrayal.*

[P100]
The moment Jin Wikyung heard his youngest brother’s words, he felt all the blood in his body run cold.

[P101]
The vague sense that something was wrong had finally taken shape.

[P102]
*Lee Seogeun’s death was where it began.*

[P103]
He had died after being poisoned with a lethal toxin. The Mount Heng Sword Sect had named the Jin Family of Taiyuan as the culprit, sparking the war.

[P104]
But the most important question had been left unanswered.

[P105]
*Who was the killer?*

[P106]
Even now, with the war nearing its end, the culprit hiding behind it all had never been identified. No—precisely because the war was nearing its end, no one cared about the killer’s identity anymore.

[P107]
Survival of the fittest. The strong would survive and claim everything.

[P108]
*This war… was wrong from the very beginning.*

[P109]
Lee Seogeun’s death.

[P110]
The unnaturally rapid spread of the rumors.

[P111]
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had declared war, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had responded. That was how the fighting had begun in earnest.

[P112]
*And the Head Elder was there.*

[P113]
The Head Elder, who had shut himself away from the world, had emerged immediately after news of Lee Seogeun’s poisoning reached the family. His role within the family had been enormous.

[P114]
A respected martial artist. A revered elder of the family.

[P115]
Without the Head Elder’s active support, the Jin Family of Taiyuan might have split in two.

[P116]
*We made it this far because of his help.*

[P117]
Then Jin Wikyung turned the thought around.

[P118]
*We made it this far because this was exactly what the Head Elder wanted.*

[P119]
In a moment too brief to even call an instant, Jin Wikyung reached his conclusion and spoke.

[P120]
“Wipeng.”

[P121]
“Your orders.”

[P122]
“Cut down the First Elder.”

[P123]
“What?”

[P124]
The stooped, emaciated old man—the First Elder—stared wide-eyed.

[P125]
The senior members nearby were equally shocked.

[P126]
“L-Lesser Family Head!”

[P127]
“What is the meaning of this…?”

[P128]
But Wipeng did not hesitate. Before anyone could react, his sword was already flying toward the First Elder’s chest.

[P129]
Clang-clang-clang!

[P130]
Two swords suddenly cut in and knocked Wipeng’s blade aside.

[P131]
Their wielders were two enormously tall, fat old men.

[P132]
They were the Second and Third Elders, who, together with the First Elder, called themselves the Head Elder’s hands and feet.

[P133]
Wipeng’s brow twitched when he saw the faint Sword Energy clinging to their blades.

[P134]
“You were hiding your martial arts.”

[P135]
The First Elder answered with a punch.

[P136]
Boom!

[P137]
The profound internal energy he had accumulated over his long life sent Wipeng flying. Then the First Elder straightened his stooped back.

[P138]
The entire field froze at the emergence of yet another Peak master, one who had spent his life hidden in the Head Elder’s shadow.

[P139]
“First Elder, what… what is this?”

[P140]
“Then could it be…?”

[P141]
*Betrayal.*

[P142]
The word stamped itself into everyone’s mind.

[P143]
“That’s impossible!”

[P144]
The White Tiger Hall Leader let out a shrill shout. If the Elders were the Head Elder’s hands and feet, then he had served faithfully as the First Elder’s.

[P145]
“Elder, Lesser Family Head. There seems to have been some misunderstanding…”

[P146]
But he never finished.

[P147]
The First Elder jerked his chin, and the Second Elder moved with blinding speed, severing the White Tiger Hall Leader’s neck.

[P148]
Shhk. Thud.

[P149]
Jin Wikyung and the First Elder locked eyes across the space between them.

[P150]
“You didn’t recruit the White Tiger Hall Leader?”

[P151]
“He was loud. That was all. The others were no different.”

[P152]
Jin Wikyung’s guess had been half right and half wrong.

[P153]
The Elders had betrayed them, but the senior members of the Elders’ faction had not.

[P154]
“Then why… Ah!”

[P155]
“Sharp. I’ll give you that.”

[P156]
The First Elder drew a dark, grimy bamboo tube from inside his robes. The fuse was already burning, and almost nothing remained.

[P157]
“How could we share such an important secret with men like them? Their job was done once they’d thrown the family into confusion. It made things easier if they had no idea what was happening outside.”

[P158]
Jin Wikyung screamed, “Stop him!”

[P159]
“You’re too late.”

[P160]
The First Elder was right.

[P161]
The moment the fuse burned to its end, something burst, and a red flame shot high into the sky.

[P162]
Fwish—boom!

[P163]
It was a signal.

[P164]
The martial artists of the small and mid-sized sects collectively known as the Five Gates of Shanxi changed in an instant—the Samdo Sect, an alliance of three sects; the saber-focused Byeokdo Sect; and the Gunggui Sect, which had been raining arrows down from the cliffs without pause.

[P165]
“Kill everyone in your path!”

[P166]
“No exceptions! Wipe them all out!”

[P167]
They were no longer the clumsy Third Rate martial artists they had pretended to be. Killing intent poured from their eyes, and their sword paths were razor-sharp.

[P168]
*This wasn’t something they prepared overnight.*

[P169]
Jin Wikyung’s expression hardened.

[P170]
* * *

[P171]
Boom!

[P172]
The Head Elder looked up at the sky. Before the red flame had even faded, thunderous shouts erupted from every direction.

[P173]
*Too fast. Far too fast.*

[P174]
The signal was supposed to be sent only after the Mount Heng Sword Sect had been annihilated. The Five Gates of Shanxi were a blade honed over decades. It had to be swung once and bring everything to a lightning-fast end.

[P175]
*All things have their proper flow.*

[P176]
The plan that had proceeded without a hitch was beginning to unravel.

[P177]
As the Head Elder smiled bitterly, a voice reached his ears.

[P178]
“So… it was you.”

[P179]
Lee Cheonbaek.

[P180]
His voice was faint, but his eyes burned more fiercely than ever.

[P181]
“You still have the strength to speak?”

[P182]
“I’ll tear you apart while you’re still alive.”

[P183]
No sooner had Lee Cheonbaek finished speaking than blood gushed from his mouth. The Head Elder pressed one of his acupoints and murmured, “That would be inconvenient just yet. You still have something to do.”

[P184]
Lee Cheonbaek despaired.

[P185]
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered heavy losses, but several hundred martial artists still remained. With its entire leadership destroyed, if the Sect Leader were now taken prisoner…

[P186]
*Just kill me!*

[P187]
The anguished cry never left his mouth. The Head Elder pressed his Mute Acupoint, robbing him of speech, then brushed the Paralysis Acupoint and turned his body rigid.

[P188]
Lee Cheonbaek had become a living corpse with his eyes wide open.

[P189]
“You bastard! Get your hands off him!”

[P190]
At the same moment, something shrieked through the air.

[P191]
Fwoooosh!

[P192]
The Head Elder did not panic. He swept his sword upward from below. Beyond the spear splitting in two along the line of his Sword Energy, Jin Taekyung was charging toward him at terrifying speed.

[P193]
“Aaaaaah!”

[P194]
“Captain! Please slow down!”

[P195]
And with him came a dozen or so riffraff who had appeared from who knew where.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 57

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃57화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“빨리, 더 빨리!”
  6|
  7|“헉, 허억!”
  8|
  9|우리는 그야말로 미친 듯이 달렸다. 혁무진은 당장 죽을 것처럼 헐떡거렸지만 죽지는 않았다. 발걸음이 느려질 때마다 등에 창날을 가져다 댔더니 적토마가 따로 없더라.
 10|
 11|그리고 어느 순간, 소리가 들리기 시작했다.
 12|
 13|누군가의 비명 소리, 철과 철이 부딪치는 소리…….
 14|
 15|다행이다. 전투는 아직 끝나지 않았다.
 16|
 17|안도감과 동시에 심장이 쿵쿵 뛰었다. 전투는 계속되고 있지만 진위경의 생사는 아직 확인하지 못했다.
 18|
 19|일 분, 일 초 차이로 그가 죽는다면?
 20|
 21|‘만약 그렇다면.’
 22|
 23|까드득.
 24|
 25|나도 모르게 창을 쥔 손에 힘이 들어갔다. 단전에서 끌어올린 공력을 두 다리로 흘려보냈다.
 26|
 27|“조, 조장!”
 28|
 29|빠르게 멀어져 가는 정찰조원들의 목소리를 뒤로하고 계속해서 달렸다. 앞서 본대가 새겨 놓은 무수한 족적, 점점 가까워지는 전장의 소음이 이정표였다.
 30|
 31|‘살아 있어라. 살아 있어라. 제발 살아…….’
 32|
 33|아! 비로소 보인다.
 34|
 35|야트막한 언덕 아래, 불과 200여 미터도 떨어지지 않은 그곳에서 수많은 무인들이 죽고 죽이는 혈전을 벌이고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“죽엇!”
 38|
 39|“으아악!”
 40|
 41|시체와 피, 그리고 더 많은 시체, 피!
 42|
 43|순간 할 말을 잃을 정도로 눈앞에 펼쳐진 광경은 잔혹했다.
 44|
 45|헌터 생활을 통해 내성을 기르지 않았다면 아마 한참 동안이나 충격에서 헤어 나오지 못했을 것이다.
 46|
 47|‘진위경! 진위경은 어디 있지?’
 48|
 49|하지만 가장 먼저 눈에 들어온 사람은 따로 있었다.
 50|
 51|멀리서도 한눈에 들어오는 백발.
 52|
 53|‘대장로!’
 54|
 55|그는 검을 들고 누군가의 앞에 서 있었다.
 56|
 57|대장로의 등에 가려 잘 보이지는 않았지만 무릎을 꿇은 그는 거구의 소유자였고, 손에는 검을 쥔 채였다.
 58|
 59|‘큰 덩치와 검?’
 60|
 61|한 사람밖에 생각나지 않았다.
 62|
 63|진위경이다. 그를 구하려면 당장 움직여야 한다.
 64|
 65|‘인벤토리 오픈.’
 66|
 67|무림에서 사용하는 인벤토리에는 온갖 물건으로 가득했다.
 68|
 69|창대는 나무로, 창두는 강철로 만들어진 이 창도 그중 하나다.
 70|
 71|‘무기 장착.’
 72|
 73|새로 꺼낸 창을 들고 뒤로 몇 걸음 물러났다.
 74|
 75|200여 미터. 까마득한 거리다. 투창으로 누군가를 맞추기에는 더더욱. 하지만 해내야 한다.
 76|
 77|‘못 할 것도 없지.’
 78|
 79|근력, 체력, 민첩.
 80|
 81|무림과 현실을 오가며 키워 온 능력치를 한껏 끌어 올렸다.
 82|
 83|공력이 깃든 팔은 창을 좀 더 멀리, 강하게 쏘아 보낼 수 있을 것이다.
 84|
 85|“후웁.”
 86|
 87|숨을 멈추고 발을 디뎠다. 첫발은 천천히, 마지막 한 걸음은 무겁게. 채찍처럼 휘두른 손끝에서 창대가 쏘아졌다.
 88|
 89|쐐애애액-!
 90|
 91|투창은 내 예상보다 빠르고 정확했다. 금방이라도 대장로의 등을 꿰뚫을 것 같았다.
 92|
 93|그런데…….
 94|
 95|서걱.
 96|
 97|‘뭐야, 저거.’
 98|
 99|푸른빛이 번쩍하더니 창이 두 쪽으로 갈라졌다. 가장 윗부분인 창두부터 끝까지, 깔끔하게.
100|
101|내가 던진 게 창인지 생일 케이크인지 헷갈릴 정도다.
102|
103|“웬 놈이냐!”
104|
105|노인네가 목청도 좋다.
106|
107|“나다, 이 십새끼야!”
108|
109|아마 대장로 평생 들어 본 적 없는 욕일 것이다.
110|
111|심지어 무림에서 그와 나는 한 집안 사람이고, 족보로 따지자면 시조새와 병아리 정도의 항렬 차이가 있다.
112|
113|이것만 해도 당황할 이유는 충분한데, 내게는 결정적인 한 방이 남아 있었다.
114|
115|“대장로는!”
116|
117|공력이 담긴 목소리가 쩌렁쩌렁 울렸다. 목소리를 낸 나도 놀랄 정도인데 다른 이들이 듣기에는 어떨까.
118|
119|저 멀리, 차가운 표정으로 굳은 그를 응시하며 있는 힘껏 외쳤다.
120|
121|“배신자다!”
122|
123|
124|
125|* * *
126|
127|
128|
129|진위경이 그 목소리를 들은 것은 항산검문의 절정 고수 세 명을 모두 쓰러트린 직후였다.
130|
131|아니, 진위경뿐만 아니라 전장의 모두가 그 외침을 들었다.
132|
133|- 웬 놈이냐!
134|
135|- 나다, 이 십새끼야!
136|
137|욕?
138|
139|전장에서는 흔한 일이다. 그러나 욕설의 대상이 대장로라면, 난데없이 나타나 쌍욕을 퍼부은 청년이 진태경이라면 이야기가 달라진다.
140|
141|“저거, 저거 삼공자 아냐?”
142|
143|“뭣? 저놈이 진태경? 그런데 왜?”
144|
145|“이게 무슨 일이야?”
146|
147|진위경도 같은 생각을 했다.
148|
149|‘무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는 거지?’
150|
151|후방에 있어야 할 막내가 전장에 나타났다. 그것만으로도 당황스러운데, 가문의 웃어른에게 입에 담지도 못할 폭언을 쓰기까지 했다. 옆에 있던 위팽이 중얼거렸다.
152|
153|“단단히 미쳤군.”
154|
155|진위경이 저도 모르게 고개를 끄덕이려던 순간.
156|
157|- 대장로는!
158|
159|더 거대한 폭탄이 떨어졌다.
160|
161|- 배신자다!
162|
163|전장이 싸늘한 침묵에 잠겼다. 간간이 들려오던 병장기 부딪치는 소리도 뚝 끊겼다.
164|
165|모두가 멍한 표정으로 진태경을 바라봤다.
166|
167|‘이게 무슨 개소리야?’
168|
169|‘배신? 대장로님께서?’
170|
171|‘취한 거 아냐? 삼공자 저거 옛날 버릇 또 튀어나오네.’
172|
173|태원진가의 무사는 말할 것도 없었고, 항산검문의 무사들도 비슷한 생각을 품었다.
174|
175|최근 들어 진태경을 좋게 보기 시작한 중진들도 입을 딱 벌렸다.
176|
177|“저런 미친놈.”
178|
179|“노야께서 어떤 분이신 줄 알고!”
180|
181|이 전쟁의 일등 공신을 꼽으라면 단연 대장로다.
182|
183|진위경을 도와 가문의 힘을 결집시켰고 오늘 전투에서는 이천백을 꺾었다.
184|
185|이처럼 이번 전쟁의 단순한 공(公)을 떠나 생각해 봐도 진태경의 말은 헛소리로 들릴 수밖에 없었다.
186|
187|대장로가 누군가?
188|
189|화양검이라 불리며 중원에까지 이름을 떨친 전대의 고수요, 정마대전에서 수많은 마두를 쓰러트린 의기의 표상이다.
190|
191|산서성의 무인이라면 누구나 그에게 크고 작은 존경심을 품고 있었다.
192|
193|“그런 분을, 뭐? 십새끼? 배신자?”
194|
195|“허어, 저놈이 태원진가 삼백 년 역사에 똥칠을 하는구나.”
196|
197|태원진가, 항산검문. 이 자리의 모두가 같은 생각을 품은 듯했다. 그러나 적어도 한 사람은 예외였다.
198|
199|‘대장로, 배신.’
200|
201|막내의 말을 들은 순간, 진위경은 온몸의 피가 싸늘하게 식는 것을 느꼈다. 그건 실체를 드러낸 위화감이었다.
202|
203|‘이소군의 죽음이 시작이었지.’
204|
205|그는 극독에 중독되어 죽었다. 항산검문은 태원진가를 범인으로 지목했고, 그것이 전쟁의 시발점이다.
206|
207|하지만 가장 중요한 의문은 빠져 있었다.
208|
209|‘흉수는 누구인가?’
210|
211|전쟁이 막바지에 이른 지금까지도 배후에 숨겨진 흉수에 대해서는 밝혀지지 않았다. 아니, 막바지에 다다랐기 때문에 아무도 흉수의 정체를 신경 쓰지 않았다.
212|
213|적자생존. 강한 자가 살아남아 모든 것을 독식할 테니까.
214|
215|‘이 전쟁은…… 처음부터 잘못된 거였어.’
216|
217|이소군의 죽음. 비상식적으로 빠른 소문의 확산.
218|
219|항산검문이 전쟁을 선언했고, 태원진가가 대응하면서 본격적인 싸움이 시작되었다.
220|
221|‘그리고 대장로가 있었다.’
222|
223|두문불출하던 대장로가 나타난 것은 이소군의 독살 소식이 전해진 직후다. 가문 내에서 그의 역할은 지대했다.
224|
225|존경받는 무인, 가문의 웃어른.
226|
227|대장로가 적극 협조하지 않았다면 태원진가는 둘로 갈라졌을지도 모른다.
228|
229|‘그의 도움 덕분에 여기까지 올 수 있었다.’
230|
231|진위경은 반대로 생각했다.
232|
233|‘여기까지 올 수 있었던 것은, 대장로가 원했기 때문이다.’
234|
235|촌각(寸刻)이라 부르지도 못할 만큼 짧은 순간. 모든 생각을 끝마친 진위경의 입이 열렸다.
236|
237|“위팽.”
238|
239|“하명하십시오.”
240|
241|“일장로를 베어라.”
242|
243|“뭐라?”
244|
245|허리가 구부정하고 깡마른 노인, 일장로가 눈을 부릅떴다.
246|
247|그뿐만 아니라 주위에 있던 중진들 모두가 깜짝 놀랐다.
248|
249|“소, 소가주!”
250|
251|“이 무슨……!”
252|
253|그러나 위팽은 망설이지 않았다. 부지불식간에 휘두른 검이 일장로의 가슴을 향해 날아갔다.
254|
255|카가가각.
256|
257|그때 갑자기 끼어든 두 개의 검이 위팽의 검을 밀어 냈다.
258|
259|뚱뚱하고 키가 훌쩍 큰 두 명의 노인.
260|
261|일장로와 함께 대장로의 수족을 자처하는 이, 삼장로였다.
262|
263|그들의 검에 맺힌 희미한 검기를 확인한 위팽의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
264|
265|“무공을 숨겼군.”
266|
267|대답 대신 일장로의 일권(一拳)이 날아왔다.
268|
269|쾅!
270|
271|살아온 세월만큼이나 심후한 공력으로 위팽을 날려 보낸 일장로가 허리를 곧게 폈다.
272|
273|평생을 대장로의 그늘에 가려져 있었던 또 다른 절정 고수의 등장에 장내가 얼어붙었다.

The sight before me was so brutal that it left me speechless.

[P22]
If my years as a Hunter hadn’t hardened me to this sort of thing, I probably would have stood there stunned for a long time.

[P23]
*Jin Wikyung! Where is Jin Wikyung?*

[P24]
But someone else caught my eye first.

[P25]
White hair, unmistakable even from this distance.

[P26]
*The Head Elder!*

[P27]
He stood before someone with a sword in his hand.

[P28]
The Head Elder’s back blocked most of my view, but the man kneeling in front of him was huge and held a sword of his own.

[P29]
*A big man with a sword?*

[P30]
Only one person came to mind.

[P31]
Jin Wikyung. If I wanted to save him, I had to act now.

[P32]
*Open Inventory.*

[P33]
My Murim Inventory was packed with all kinds of things.

[P34]
The spear I pulled out was one of them, with a wooden shaft and a steel head.

[P35]
*Equip Weapon.*

[P36]
Spear in hand, I took several steps back.

[P37]
Two hundred meters. An impossibly long distance—especially if I was trying to hit someone with a thrown spear.

[P38]
But I had to do it.

[P39]
*No reason I can’t.*

[P40]
Strength, Stamina, Agility.

[P41]
I pushed the stats I’d built up traveling between Murim and reality to their limits.

[P42]
The internal energy coursing through my arm would send the spear farther and faster.

[P43]
“Hup.”

[P44]
I held my breath and stepped forward. The first step was slow, the final step heavy. My arm snapped out like a whip, and the spear shot from my fingertips.

[P45]
Fwoooosh!

[P46]
The throw was faster and more accurate than I’d expected. It looked ready to punch straight through the Head Elder’s back.

[P47]
But then…

[P48]
Shhk.

[P49]
*What the hell was that?*

[P50]
Blue light flashed, and the spear split cleanly in two from the tip of the spearhead to the end of the shaft.

[P51]
I couldn’t tell whether I’d thrown a spear or a birthday cake.

[P52]
“Who the hell are you?”

[P53]
The old man had quite a set of lungs.

[P54]
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”

[P55]
That was probably the first time in the Head Elder’s life anyone had cursed him like that.

[P56]
To make matters worse, he and I belonged to the same family in Murim. Going by the family tree, the difference in seniority between us was roughly that of an archaeopteryx and a chick.

[P57]
That alone was plenty of reason for him to be stunned, but I still had one finishing blow left.

[P58]
“The Head Elder is—!”

[P59]
My voice, loaded with internal energy, thundered across the battlefield. Even I was startled by how loud it was. I could only imagine what it sounded like to everyone else.

[P60]
I stared at his cold, frozen face in the distance and shouted with all my might.

[P61]
“A traitor!”

[P62]
* * *

[P63]
Jin Wikyung heard the voice immediately after bringing down all three Peak masters of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.

[P64]
No, it wasn’t just him. Everyone on the battlefield heard the shout.

[P65]
“Who the hell are you?”

[P66]
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”

[P67]
Cursing?

[P68]
That was common enough on a battlefield. But it was a different matter when the target was the Head Elder and the young man who had appeared out of nowhere to hurl such abuse at him was Jin Taekyung.

[P69]
“Isn’t that… the Third Young Master?”

[P70]
“What? That’s Jin Taekyung? But why?”

[P71]
“What’s going on?”

[P72]
Jin Wikyung was wondering the same thing.

[P73]
*What in the world is happening?*

[P74]
His youngest brother, who should have been in the rear, had appeared on the battlefield. That alone was bewildering enough, but now he was hurling unspeakable abuse at one of the family’s most senior elders.

[P75]
Wipeng, standing beside him, muttered, “He’s completely lost his mind.”

[P76]
Jin Wikyung was about to nod without thinking when—

[P77]
“The Head Elder is—!”

[P78]
An even bigger bomb dropped.

[P79]
“A traitor!”

[P80]
An icy silence fell over the battlefield. Even the sporadic clash of weapons came to an abrupt stop.

[P81]
Everyone stared blankly at Jin Taekyung.

[P82]
*What kind of bullshit is this?*

[P83]
*Betrayal? The Head Elder?*

[P84]
*Is he drunk? The Third Young Master must be slipping back into his old habits.*

[P85]
The martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan naturally thought so, and those of the Mount Heng Sword Sect were no different.

[P86]
Even the senior members who had recently begun to think better of Jin Taekyung gaped at him.

[P87]
“What a lunatic.”

[P88]
“Does he have any idea who the Old Master is?”

[P89]
If anyone deserved the most credit for this war, it was undoubtedly the Head Elder.

[P90]
He had helped Jin Wikyung unite the family’s forces, and in today’s battle, he had defeated Lee Cheonbaek.

[P91]
Even setting aside his contributions to the war, Jin Taekyung’s claim could only sound absurd.

[P92]
Who was the Head Elder?

[P93]
He was a master of the previous generation whose title, the Blade of Flowers, was renowned even across the Central Plains. He was a symbol of righteousness who had struck down countless fiends during the Great Faction War.

[P94]
Every martial artist in Shanxi held some measure of respect for him.

[P95]
“That man? A son of a bitch? A traitor?”

[P96]
“Good heavens. That boy is smearing shit over the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s three-hundred-year history.”

[P97]
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect—everyone present seemed to share the same thought.

[P98]
With at least one exception.

[P99]
*The Head Elder. Betrayal.*

[P100]
The moment Jin Wikyung heard his youngest brother’s words, he felt all the blood in his body run cold.

[P101]
The vague sense that something was wrong had finally taken shape.

[P102]
*Lee Seogeun’s death was where it began.*

[P103]
He had died after being poisoned with a lethal toxin. The Mount Heng Sword Sect had named the Jin Family of Taiyuan as the culprit, sparking the war.

[P104]
But the most important question had been left unanswered.

[P105]
*Who was the killer?*

[P106]
Even now, with the war nearing its end, the culprit hiding behind it all had never been identified. No—precisely because the war was nearing its end, no one cared about the killer’s identity anymore.

[P107]
Survival of the fittest. The strong would survive and claim everything.

[P108]
*This war… was wrong from the very beginning.*

[P109]
Lee Seogeun’s death.

[P110]
The unnaturally rapid spread of the rumors.

[P111]
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had declared war, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had responded. That was how the fighting had begun in earnest.

[P112]
*And the Head Elder was there.*

[P113]
The Head Elder, who had shut himself away from the world, had emerged immediately after news of Lee Seogeun’s poisoning reached the family. His role within the family had been enormous.

[P114]
A respected martial artist. A revered elder of the family.

[P115]
Without the Head Elder’s active support, the Jin Family of Taiyuan might have split in two.

[P116]
*We made it this far because of his help.*

[P117]
Then Jin Wikyung turned the thought around.

[P118]
*We made it this far because this was exactly what the Head Elder wanted.*

[P119]
In a moment too brief to even call an instant, Jin Wikyung reached his conclusion and spoke.

[P120]
“Wipeng.”

[P121]
“Your orders.”

[P122]
“Cut down the First Elder.”

[P123]
“What?”

[P124]
The stooped, emaciated old man—the First Elder—stared wide-eyed.

[P125]
The senior members nearby were equally shocked.

[P126]
“L-Lesser Family Head!”

[P127]
“What is the meaning of this…?”

[P128]
But Wipeng did not hesitate. Before anyone could react, his sword was already flying toward the First Elder’s chest.

[P129]
Clang-clang-clang!

[P130]
Two swords suddenly cut in and knocked Wipeng’s blade aside.

[P131]
Their wielders were two enormously tall, fat old men.

[P132]
They were the Second and Third Elders, who, together with the First Elder, called themselves the Head Elder’s hands and feet.

[P133]
Wipeng’s brow twitched when he saw the faint Sword Energy clinging to their blades.

[P134]
“You were hiding your martial arts.”

[P135]
The First Elder answered with a punch.

[P136]
Boom!

[P137]
The profound internal energy he had accumulated over his long life sent Wipeng flying. Then the First Elder straightened his stooped back.

[P138]
The entire field froze at the emergence of yet another Peak master, one who had spent his life hidden in the Head Elder’s shadow.

[P139]
“First Elder, what… what is this?”

[P140]
“Then could it be…?”

[P141]
*Betrayal.*

[P142]
The word stamped itself into everyone’s mind.

[P143]
“That’s impossible!”

[P144]
The White Tiger Hall Leader let out a shrill shout. If the Elders were the Head Elder’s hands and feet, then he had served faithfully as the First Elder’s.

[P145]
“Elder, Lesser Family Head. There seems to have been some misunderstanding…”

[P146]
But he never finished.

[P147]
The First Elder jerked his chin, and the Second Elder moved with blinding speed, severing the White Tiger Hall Leader’s neck.

[P148]
Shhk. Thud.

[P149]
Jin Wikyung and the First Elder locked eyes across the space between them.

[P150]
“You didn’t recruit the White Tiger Hall Leader?”

[P151]
“He was loud. That was all. The others were no different.”

[P152]
Jin Wikyung’s guess had been half right and half wrong.

[P153]
The Elders had betrayed them, but the senior members of the Elders’ faction had not.

[P154]
“Then why… Ah!”

[P155]
“Sharp. I’ll give you that.”

[P156]
The First Elder drew a dark, grimy bamboo tube from inside his robes. The fuse was already burning, and almost nothing remained.

[P157]
“How could we share such an important secret with men like them? Their job was done once they’d thrown the family into confusion. It made things easier if they had no idea what was happening outside.”

[P158]
Jin Wikyung screamed, “Stop him!”

[P159]
“You’re too late.”

[P160]
The First Elder was right.

[P161]
The moment the fuse burned to its end, something burst, and a red flame shot high into the sky.

[P162]
Fwish—boom!

[P163]
It was a signal.

[P164]
The martial artists of the small and mid-sized sects collectively known as the Five Gates of Shanxi changed in an instant—the Samdo Sect, an alliance of three sects; the saber-focused Byeokdo Sect; and the Gunggui Sect, which had been raining arrows down from the cliffs without pause.

[P165]
“Kill everyone in your path!”

[P166]
“No exceptions! Wipe them all out!”

[P167]
They were no longer the clumsy Third Rate martial artists they had pretended to be. Killing intent poured from their eyes, and their sword paths were razor-sharp.

[P168]
*This wasn’t something they prepared overnight.*

[P169]
Jin Wikyung’s expression hardened.

[P170]
* * *

[P171]
Boom!

[P172]
The Head Elder looked up at the sky. Before the red flame had even faded, thunderous shouts erupted from every direction.

[P173]
*Too fast. Far too fast.*

[P174]
The signal was supposed to be sent only after the Mount Heng Sword Sect had been annihilated. The Five Gates of Shanxi were a blade honed over decades. It had to be swung once and bring everything to a lightning-fast end.

[P175]
*All things have their proper flow.*

[P176]
The plan that had proceeded without a hitch was beginning to unravel.

[P177]
As the Head Elder smiled bitterly, a voice reached his ears.

[P178]
“So… it was you.”

[P179]
Lee Cheonbaek.

[P180]
His voice was faint, but his eyes burned more fiercely than ever.

[P181]
“You still have the strength to speak?”

[P182]
“I’ll tear you apart while you’re still alive.”

[P183]
No sooner had Lee Cheonbaek finished speaking than blood gushed from his mouth. The Head Elder pressed one of his acupoints and murmured, “That would be inconvenient just yet. You still have something to do.”

[P184]
Lee Cheonbaek despaired.

[P185]
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered heavy losses, but several hundred martial artists still remained. With its entire leadership destroyed, if the Sect Leader were now taken prisoner…

[P186]
*Just kill me!*

[P187]
The anguished cry never left his mouth. The Head Elder pressed his Mute Acupoint, robbing him of speech, then brushed the Paralysis Acupoint and turned his body rigid.

[P188]
Lee Cheonbaek had become a living corpse with his eyes wide open.

[P189]
“You bastard! Get your hands off him!”

[P190]
At the same moment, something shrieked through the air.

[P191]
Fwoooosh!

[P192]
The Head Elder did not panic. He swept his sword upward from below. Beyond the spear splitting in two along the line of his Sword Energy, Jin Taekyung was charging toward him at terrifying speed.

[P193]
“Aaaaaah!”

[P194]
“Captain! Please slow down!”

[P195]
And with him came a dozen or so riffraff who had appeared from who knew where.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
